rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: We seek $2.5M to develop a multi-use innovation and co-working space dedicated to small business support, training in e-commerce and digital tools, incubation for MWBEs, and access to capital networks. The hub would serve as a central location for mentorship, technical assistance, and job creation.
rows.headline: Other capital budget request for SBS
rows.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency supports but cannot accommodate Explanation: SBS does not have funding to expand our Business Solution Centers at this time. SBS is proud to offer, both virtually and in-person at our Business Solutions Centers, businesses 1-1 support, courses and webinars, support in accessing capital, and free legal services. Though not a co-working space, our Business Solutions offer entrepreneurs connections to free services to start, operate, and grow their business. Connections include support for M/WBE certification and mentorship networks. SBS offers the M/WBE Mentors program, a peer mentorship program for NYC M/WBEs. These mentors provide insight to M/WBEs needed to succeed and chart their own path of growth through government contracting our business education offering, we offer free business courses/webinars to help businesses develop their marketing and promotional skills. We encourage any entrepreneurs interested in receiving support to call our Small Business Hotline, 888-SBS-4NYC. SBS is always open to exploring new programming, including an incubator programming pending availablity of resources.

rows.explanation: Newly opened small businesses will need to re-evaluate how to conduct business while adhering to new public health measures. For many of them, converting to digital advertising and shipping will be anything but avoidable. Many of the small businesses in our district have been in existence for decades and before the pandemic, were able to survive under the old model, However due to a variety in language barriers and technological competencies, many business owners may need training to learn new marketing techniques in how to continue operating through a second wave and post pandemic.

rows.headline: Other commercial district revitalization requests
rows.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: This request has already been completed. Explanation: SBS provides opportunities for local CBOs to take on commercial revitalization efforts on commercial corridors across the city. For instance, in the last two years, SBS awarded Bangladeshi American Community Development & Youth Services (BACDYS) a public realm grants of $50,000 to design and implement new art murals and public space improvements in Ozone Park. In addition, SBS also provided $60,000 grant to BACDYS to conduct merchant organizing in the neighborhood and form a local merchant association. SBS will continue to promote grant programs when available and encourage the community boards to share information about our grant programs with local non-profits.
